naslov: Three Things That Lead a Man to Ruin

segmenti.tekst: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين.

قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. أَمَّا بَعْدُ. Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), our Prophet, upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah

of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Dear brothers, respected members of the congregation, a believer in this world is tested with various trials, as has been announced to us by the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Ahasiban-nasu an yutraku an yaqulu amanna" – do people think that they will be left alone because they say "we believe" – we believe in Allah and His Messenger –

and that they will not be tested? Sometimes these trials are smaller, sometimes greater, but there are trials that can lead a person to ruin. So we can say that the ruin of a person, as the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, foretold to us in his hadiths, lies in three things.

The first thing, dear brothers, is secret sins, sins that a person commits in secret, when he thinks that no one sees him. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says that on the Day of Judgement a person will come "bi hasanatin amthali jibali Tihamah," that he will come with good deeds, when people are gathered on the Day of Judgement. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "I will recognise them."

I know these people; they will come with good deeds as great as the mountains of Tihamah. And the mountains of Tihamah are a huge chain of mountains stretching along the coast of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Peninsula, along the entire coast, a huge chain of mountains.

So a person will come on the Day of Judgement with so many good deeds, which will be white, the Prophet says, white. And then, he says, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "fa yaj'aluhullahu haba'an manthura."

And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, he says, will turn them into dust. "Haba'an manthura" – if you know, brothers, it is when the sun comes into our homes through the windows and you can see that fine dust that is barely visible to the naked eye. That is what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will make of the good deeds of those people; that is, He will destroy them. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: Allah will turn them into dust. Thawban, who narrates the hadith, asked: "O Messenger," he said, "O Messenger, describe these people to us,

who these people are, so that we are not among them without even knowing it." "They are your brothers, your Muslim brothers, of your own skin, of the children of Adam; these people are not jinn, but they are people – people who, when they are alone, when they think no one sees them, transgress Allah's limits, violate Allah's prohibitions."

And this hadith is so relevant in our time, dear brothers, that it is unbelievable. That a person today, in our time, can commit as much haram in an hour as he could not have committed in a year a hundred years ago.

That a person, by means of mobile phones, can commit as much haram in a single hour as he could not have committed in a year 100 or 200 years ago. So this hadith warns us how dangerous secret sins are. Because this is a form of hypocrisy: that a person shows people his good side, but when he is alone, within his own four walls, he does what Allah is not pleased with.

So a person should be afraid. And this hadith is terrifying, dear brothers, terrifying, and a person should take a lesson from it, especially in our time. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, further says – that is, the second ruin of a person is the trial of money.

The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Inna li kulli ummatin fitnatan" – truly every ummah, every nation, the earlier nations, he says, had their trials – "wa inna fitnata ummati al-mal" – he says: and truly the trial of my ummah is what? Money. The accumulation of money. "Wa tuhibbunal-mala hubban jamma" – and you love wealth…
So among the trials of this ummah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is money. That a person is no longer content with having enough, but wants to have even more than he needs.
It is not a problem when a person has money and spends it on that which pleases Allah. But when a person spends it on that which does not please Allah, then there is a problem.

That is when the main problem arises. Why is money such a trial? Because it is a means to other sins. When a person has money, he will commit fornication, and haram, and gambling, and alcohol, and everything.

The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says in a hadith recorded by both Bukhari and Muslim: "By Allah," he says, "I do not fear for you that you will," he says, "fall into shirk, into polytheism; rather, I fear," he says, "for you that you will compete with one another for this world,

and be ruined as those before you were ruined." You will see the Arab countries today – we see how they have fallen precisely because of that money; their generations of young people have been ruined precisely because of that money, because of that prosperity. What do they do? They just pile up money. And people already have plans for the next 500 years.

And the situation is no better here at home either, dear brothers. You will see that those who hold these towns of ours here have the town wrapped around their little finger, but what do they want? They want every person, every human being, to be under their control, that is, just to collect, collect as much money as possible.
And then we see that these are our brothers who pray together with us in the same row. But, unfortunately, money is a trial.
"Truly, your wealth and your children – they are your trial," says Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

And it is very beautiful when a person directs that money where it should go: to the poor, to the needy, and so on, and so forth. And because of that money he earns Jannah (Paradise). The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says – this is the third thing, the third ruin for a person – it is, dear brothers, the trial of women.
It is the trial of women. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "This world is sweet and green. Allah has made you successors in this world to see how you will" – what? – "act."
How a person will act in this world. He further says: "Fattaqud-dunya" – he says: beware of this world. What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? Beware of this world.

Guard yourselves against this world. "Fala taghurrannakumul-hayatud-dunya," says Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – so let not the life of this world deceive you. Short, very short. Its blessings are passing.

"Wattaqun-nisa'" – and he says: beware of, or guard yourselves against, women. "Fa inna awwala fitnati Bani Isra'ila kanat fin-nisa'" – for the first trial of the Children of Israel, the sons or descendants of Ya'qub, was in what?
In women. Why? Because, dear brothers, a wife can sometimes drive a man to abandon obedience to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. In what way? Through great demands.

Sometimes a man, in order to please his wife, works two jobs. He has no time for the mosque, nor for the congregation, nor for Allah. He has no time for the One who created time. Especially these younger generations.
Those who have just got married, and in order to please his wife, to take her to the Maldives, to Italy, to Turkey, on a summer holiday, a man breaks himself.

Also, when a woman goes out exposed and mixes with men, what comes of it? It comes to that, it comes to fornication, to zina, to great trials. And of course, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will not grant such people istiqamah (steadfastness), He will not grant it.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, does not let a fornicator remain on the straight path; rather, He turns him away from the straight path, precisely because of that great sin. And fornication is one of the greatest and worst, the worst of sins, the most abhorrent sin.

That is why a person should fear these sins, guard himself against these sins, these trials, because in them lies ruin for a person and for the whole of society. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to help us be among those who will have istiqamah on the straight path. I ask Him, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to admit us into Jannah. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'anil-'azim, wa nafa'ani wa iyyakum bima fihi minal-ayati wadh-dhikril-hakim. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwal-Ghafurur-Rahim.
